title: CDRThief_Investigation_4c3
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected compromise involving the CDRThief malware on a VoIP platform. The malware is known to target specific VoIP platforms and exfiltrate call detail records (CDR). Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected compromise involving the CDRThief malware on a VoIP platform. The malware is known to target specific VoIP platforms and exfiltrate call detail records (CDR). Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the provided credentials.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service is `bkd.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified a suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. This will help you understand the persistence mechanism used by the malware.
levels.solution: Investigate systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service. Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers. The persistence mechanism is `lab-checkin.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to list all timers.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication to help contain the threat.
levels.solution: Analyze network connections and look for any unusual outbound traffic. Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections. The C2 port number is `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Analyze network connections and look for any unusual outbound traffic.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all network connections.
